'''Nancy Burgess Hingston''' is a mathematician working in [[algebraic topology]] and [[differential geometry]]. She is a professor emerita of mathematics at [[The College of New Jersey]].<ref name="profile">{{citation|url=http://science.tcnj.edu/school-information/women-in-science/dr-nancy-hingston/|title=Dr. Nancy Hingston|work=Women in Science: Profiles of Selected TCNJ Women Faculty and Alumni|publisher=School of Science, [[The College of New Jersey]]|accessdate=2015-10-25}}.</ref>

==Early life and education==
Nancy Hingston's father William Hingston was superintendent of the [[Central Bucks School District]] in Pennsylvania; her mother was a high school mathematics and computer science teacher.<ref name="wedding"/> She graduated from the [[University of Pennsylvania]] with a double major in [[mathematics]] and [[physics]]. After a year studying physics as a graduate student, she switched to mathematics,<ref name="profile"/> and completed her PhD in 1981 from [[Harvard University]] under the supervision of [[Raoul Bott]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=79364}}</ref>

==Career==
Before joining TCNJ, she taught at the University of Pennsylvania.<ref name="wedding"/> She has also been a frequent visitor to the [[Institute for Advanced Study]],<ref name="profile"/> and has been involved with the Program for Women and Mathematics at the Institute for Advanced Study since its founding in 1994.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.nj.com/mercer/index.ssf/2012/05/mentoring_young_women_is_integ.html|first=Wendy|last=Plump|date=May 29, 2012|title=Mentoring young women is integral to institute's math program|newspaper=[[The Times (Trenton)|Times of Trenton]]}}.</ref>

==Contributions==
Nancy Hingston made major contributions in Riemannian geometry and Hamiltonian dynamics, and more specifically in the study of [[closed geodesic]]s and, more generally, [[periodic orbits]] of Hamiltonian systems. In her very first paper,<ref>{{citation|first=Nancy|last=Hingston|title= Equivariant Morse theory and closed geodesics | journal=[[Journal of Differential Geometry]]|volume=19| year=1984| issue=1 | pages=85–116| doi=10.4310/jdg/1214438424|doi-access=free}}</ref> she proved that a generic [[Riemannian metric]] on a closed manifold possesses infinitely many closed geodesics. In the 1990s, she proved that the growth rate of [[closed geodesics]] in Riemannian 2-spheres is at least the one of prime numbers.<ref>{{citation|first=Nancy|last=Hingston|title= On the growth of the number of closed geodesics on the two-sphere| journal=[[International Mathematics Research Notices]]|volume=1993| year=1993| issue=9 | pages=253–262| doi=10.1155/S1073792893000285|doi-access=free }}</ref> In the years 2000s, she proved the long-standing [[Conley conjecture]] from symplectic geometry: every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a standard symplectic torus of any even dimension possesses infinitely many periodic points<ref>{{citation|first=Nancy|last=Hingston|title= Subharmonic solutions of Hamiltonian equations on tori| journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=170| year=2009| issue=2 | pages=529–560| doi=10.4007/annals.2009.170.529|doi-access=free}}</ref> (the result was subsequently extended by [[Viktor Ginzburg]] to more general [[symplectic manifolds]]).

==Recognition==
Nancy Hingston was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2014.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|accessdate=2015-10-01|archive-date=2017-11-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref name="tcnj-icm">{{citation|url=https://news.tcnj.edu/2014/05/26/on-stage-in-seoul/|first=Mary Jo|last=Patterson|title=On Stage in Seoul|date=May 26, 2014|work=TCJN News|publisher=[[The College of New Jersey]]|accessdate=2015-10-25}}.</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Hingston, Nancy|chapter=Loop products, Poincaré duality, index growth and dynamics|volume=2|title=Proceedings of the ICM, Seoul 2014|pages=881–896}}</ref>

She is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], for "contributions to differential geometry and the study of closed geodesics."<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows 2017 Class of the Fellows of the AMS], [[American Mathematical Society]], retrieved 2016-11-06.</ref>

==Personal==
Her husband, Jovi Tenev, is a lawyer.<ref name="wedding">{{citation|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1981/08/23/style/jovi-tenev-weds-nancy-hingston.html|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|title=Jovi Tenev Weds Nancy Hingston|department=Style|date=August 23, 1981}}.</ref> She has three children.<ref name="tcnj-icm"/>
